 Oral Judgment
(Per: Hon'Ble Mr. Justice Ramachandra D. Huddar)

The appellant - Nekrtc,
represented by its Managing Director, Kalaburagi has questioned the quantum of compensation
awarded vide judgment and award dated 15.07.2022 in Mvc No.280/2021 by the Mact,
Lingasugur.
2. Parties to this appeal are referred with reference to their ranking before the Tribunal.

3.  It is the case of the claimants before the Tribunal, that on 01.11.2020 at about 8.00 p.m., the complainant and deceased Bhimanna were proceeding on a motor cycle and at that time, a bus bearing Reg.No.KA-36/T-1135 came from Raichur road driven by its driver in a rash and negligent manner endangering human life and dashed to Bhimanna.
Because of this impact, Bhimanna sustained injuries on his person and died on the spot.
It is the case of the claimants that claimant No.1 is the mother of the deceased, claimant Nos.2 and 3 are his sisters.
They were depending upon the income of the deceased.
It is claimed by the claimants that during his lifetime deceased was a Barber by profession and NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB was earning Rs.30,000/- per month.

As the said accident has taken place because of the rash and negligent driving of the NEKRTC bus by its driver, both the respondents so stated in the cause-title are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
Hence, it is prayed to award a compensation of Rs.35,00,000/- under all the relevant heads.
4. Pursuant to the notice issued by the Tribunal, despite service of notice, respondent No.1 has not appeared before the Tribunal.
Therefore, he was placed exparte.
Respondent No.2 appeared and resisted the petition by fling detailed objection statement denying the entire assertions made in the petition.
It is contended that the rider of the motor cycle was not possessing driving license.
Respondent No.2 has paid the interim compensation of Rs.25,000/- to the claimants.
There is clear violation of provision of Section 121 of M.V. Act.
As two vehicles involved in the said accident, it is contended that there was a contributory negligence on the part of the rider of the motor cycle also.
Hence, amongst other grounds, it is prayed by the respondent No.2 to dismiss the petition.
Based upon the rival pleadings of both the parties, the learned Tribunal framed three relevant issues.
6. Before the Tribunal, to prove the case of the claimants, Virupamma i.e., claimant No.1 the mother of the deceased entered the witness box as PW-1.
She has produced Ex.P-1 to P-8 and closed claimants' evidence.

To rebut the evidence of the claimants, respondent No.2 examined Jakeer The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75073881/
3

entities.text: Jakeer The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Hussain S/o Khadarsab as RW-1.
He is none else than respondent No.1 so arrayed in the claim petition.
On behalf of the respondent No.2, Ex.R-1 payment receipt is marked.

7. Learned Tribunal, on hearing the arguments and on evaluation of the evidence awarded compensation under the following heads:
Loss of income due to the Rs.20,79,000.00 death of deceased Loss of consortium Rs.40,000.00
Loss of estate Rs.15,000.00 Funeral expenses Rs.15,000.00 Total Rs.21,49,000.00 8.
Thus, the Tribunal held that the claimants are entitled for total compensation of Rs.21,49,000/-.

This is how now the appellant is before this Court challenging the quantum of compensation on the ground that the deceased as per the NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB admission of PW-1 in the cross-examination was aged 17 years and he was a minor.
9. Learned counsel Smt. Preeti Patil Melkundi submits that in view of the admission of PW-1 with regard to the age, whatever the notional income being taken by the Tribunal is incorrect.
The global compensation ought to have been awarded because of the death of the deceased minor in the accident.
She further submits that rider of the motor cycle was not possessing driving license and even there is violation of policy condition by the owner.
Therefore, she prays to interfere in the award passed by the Tribunal by allowing this appeal.

10. As against this submission, the learned counsel for the claimants, with all force, submits that,
though PW-1 has stated with regard to the age of the deceased as 17 years, but she is a rustic villager.
She has not told the exact age of the deceased.
Deceased was a Barber by profession.
As per the police documents so produced i.e., FIR, charge sheet postmortem report, the age of the deceased is shown as 18 years.
Therefore, the said admission of PW-1 so relied upon by the learned counsel for the appellant has no force.

He further NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB submits that as the deceased was Barber by profession, he was earning more than Rs.30,000/- per month but even then, the Tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.13,750/- as per the chart prepared by the KSLSA.
But the claimants have not filed any separate appeal challenging the said award as it is on the lower side.
11. We have given our anxious consideration for the arguments on both side.

12. Though it is submitted by the learned counsel for the appellant that, in view of the admission of PW-1 the Tribunal ought to have taken the age of the deceased as 17 years, but the submission of the counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted for the simple reason that when the complaint was lodged with regard to the said accident of the complainant, the age of the deceased was shown as 18 years.
While conducting the postmortem the doctor has opined that deceased was aged 18 years.
In the charge sheet also the age of the deceased is shown as 18 years.

In view of these documentary evidence which were marked in evidence before the Tribunal through PW-1, at the time of marking those NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB documents, no little finger was raised by the appellant - respondent No.2.
For the first time such a contention is taken in this appeal.

As the documentary evidence prevails over the oral evidence, PW-1 being the rustic villager, might have deposed the age The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75073881/
4 of the deceased on imagination.

entities.text: Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, the argument of the counsel for the appellant that the deceased was aged 17 years at the time of the accident cannot be accepted.

13. So far as the contributory negligence on the part of the deceased as contended by the appellant is concerned, it is pleaded by the claimants in the petition that the complainant as well as deceased went to bring the articles and they stopped their motor cycle near Manju Petrol Bunk at Kavital, the complainant has gone to bring materials to a shop.
At that time the NEKRTC bus driver by driving the bus in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased because of that accident Bhimanna died on the spot itself.
This fact of accident is not disputed.
It is not the case of the respondent No.2 that at the time of accident deceased was really riding the said motor cycle.

The argument of the learned counsel for the appellant cannot be accepted for the simple reason that NC:
2024:KHC-K:6924-DB deceased was not driving the said vehicle at the time of accident as per the pleadings so pleaded by the claimants in the petition.

No such evidence is coming forth from the mouth of either respondent No.2 or RW-1 who was the driver of the said vehicle at the time of accident. RW-1 who was driver of the said vehicle at the relevant time would have been the best witness to say as to how the accident has taken place.
Except the pleadings and bald submissions at the time or argument, there is no evidence placed on record by the appellant either before the Tribunal or before this Court.
Further it is submitted that there was contributory negligence on the part of rider of the motor cycle.
But no such evidence is placed on record by respondent No.2 by effectively cross examining PW-1.
In the absence of acceptable evidence, the grounds with regard to contributory negligence falls to the ground.

14. So far as quantum of compensation is concerned, the Tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased as 18 years by relying upon the judgment of Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1 the proper 2009(6) SCC 121 - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB multiplier was taken into consideration.

entities.text: Sarla Verma vs. Delhi Transport Corporation1 the proper 2009(6) SCC 121 - 10 - NC: 2024
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So also the Tribunal has assessed the income as per the chart prepared by the KSLSA at Rs.13,750/- per month.
Though the claimants have contended that the deceased was earning Rs.30,000/- per month, except bald pleading, no documentary evidence is produced by the claimants .
Therefore, the Tribunal is right in taking the income of the deceased at Rs.13,750/- per month as per the chart of KSLSA.

As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others2 40% of the income has to be added towards future prospects of the deceased.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi and Others2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: So 40% of Rs.13,750/- comes to Rs.5,500/-.
Thus the total income of the deceased is worked out at Rs.13,750/- + Rs.5,500/- = Rs.19,250/-.
The deceased was a bachelor.
As per the judgment of Sarla Verma's case (supra) 50% of the total income has to be deducted towards his personal expenses.
Thus, the income of the deceased is worked out at Rs.19,250 - Rs.9625 = Rs.9,625/-.
It is to be multiplied with 12.

As the age of the deceased was 18 years at the time of accident, as per the judgment of Sarla Verma's case (supra) (2017) 16 SCC 680 The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75073881/
5 - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB the proper multiplier that is applicable is '18'.

entities.text: Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Thus, the loss of dependency is worked out at Rs.9,625 x 12 x 18 = Rs.20,79,000/-.
The Tribunal has rightly calculated the said loss of dependency at Rs.20,79,000/-.
The claimants being the mother, has lost her son.

Since there is loss of consortium, as per the judgment of Pranay Sethi's case (supra)
towards loss of consortium Rs.40,000/- is awarded by the Tribunal so also towards loss of estate and towards funeral expenses, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/-.

In our opinion whatever the compensation so awarded by the Tribunal is held to be correct and it is just and fair compensation awarded by the Tribunal which do not require any interference by this Court.

15. So far as interest is concerned, the claimants have claimed interest at the rate of 12% but considering the present day conditions as well as prevailing bank rate interest, the Tribunal has awarded interest at 6% per annum.
In our opinion, awarding of interest on the said amount is correct which do not require any interference.

16. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that in view of the judgment of the Co-ordinate bench of this Court - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB in Chandrakala & Anr. vs. Dilipkumar M.A. & Anr. in MFA No.1662/2022 disposed of on 02.07.2024, the claimants are not entitled for any interest on the future prospects.

entities.text: Chandrakala & Anr. vs. Dilipkumar M.A. & Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As rightly submitted by the counsel for the appellant, claimants are not entitled for interest on the future prospects.

Therefore, the appeal filed by the appellant deserves to be allowed in part holding that the Tribunal is right in awarding compensation but however the claimants are not entitled for interest on the future prospects.
While calculating interest, the Tribunal is directed not to calculate the interest on the future prospects.

Resultantly, we pass the following:
ORDER
(i) The appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The judgment and award dated 15.07.2022 passed by the Tribunal in MVC No.280/2021 by the MACT, Lingasugur is hereby confirmed.
However, the claimants are held not entitled for interest on the future prospects.

(iii) The Tribunal is directed not to calculate interest on the future prospects while - 13 -  NC: 2024:KHC-K:6924-DB The Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors on 13 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/75073881/
6  calculating interest at the time of  disbursement.

entities.text: Managing Director Nekrtc vs Virupamma And Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: (iv) The other portion of the order passed by the Tribunal remains unaltered.
The Registry is directed to transmit the statutory deposit to the Tribunal forthwith.
Send back the Trial Court records along with copy of this judgment.
